bibliographic.authors: Emmanuel Cadet; Edima David Etim; Iboro Akpan Essien; Eseoghene Daniel Erigha; Lawal Abdulmutalib Babatunde; Joshua Oluwagbenga Ajayi; Ehimah Obuse

methodology.study_design: exploratory study with case studies and simulated enterprise performance evaluation mentioned in abstract; full methods not provided in excerpt
methodology.sector: cybersecurity; IT and operational technology environments
methodology.technology_context: LLMs integrated with SIEM systems for policy analysis, regulatory interpretation, compliance monitoring, and risk assessment

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article directly addresses LLMs for policy compliance, regulatory interpretation, risk mitigation, governance, monitoring, and human oversight in regulated cybersecurity contexts (GDPR, HIPAA, NIST, ISO 27001). However, the provided text contains no evidence of conversational systems, chatbots, agents, RAG, or conversational governance, which is the core scope of the review. It is relevant as supporting evidence on LLM governance/compliance/risk rather than central conversational-governance evidence.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial introduction/literature review were provided; automated triage marked it central despite zero conversational-AI matches; full-text verification needed for study design, case studies, and empirical claims.

appraisal.notes: Abstract clearly states aims and claimed contributions, including case studies and simulated enterprise evaluation, but the provided excerpt does not describe sampling, data collection procedures, analysis methods, or ethics. Appraisal is therefore limited and conservative.

cerqual.explanation: The abstract presents a coherent argument linking LLMs to compliance and risk mitigation in regulated environments, but methodological detail is absent in the supplied text. Relevance to the review is partial: strong on governance/compliance/risk with LLMs, weak on conversational governance.

coding.theme: LLM-supported cybersecurity policy compliance and risk mitigation
coding.subtheme: Regulatory mapping, monitoring, and governance controls in regulated IT/OT environments

synthesis.main_claim: LLMs can automate policy analysis, monitor adherence to standards, support real-time risk assessment, and serve as dynamic compliance advisors when integrated with systems such as SIEM, while challenges include interpretability, hallucinations, and data privacy.
synthesis.contribution: Positions LLMs as tools for translating regulatory frameworks into technical controls, improving compliance mapping accuracy, reducing false positives versus rule-based systems, and supporting collaborative AI-human governance in complex regulated environments.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text notes challenges with interpretability, domain-specific fine-tuning, hallucinations, and securing sensitive data during inference; detailed study limitations are not available in the excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Include as supporting evidence for LLM governance, compliance automation, risk mitigation, monitoring, and human oversight in regulated/high-stakes settings; do not treat as central evidence for conversational governance because no conversational-AI application is described.
